# Configuration reference

Generated from `defaults/config.yaml`. The comments in that file are the documentation — update them there and regenerate this page.

## `config_version`

**Default:** `1.2`

## `config_advanced`

This key is managed by the Web GUI and has no effect on the backend. Do NOT change it manually unless you know what you are doing.

**Default:** `false`

## `auto_update_config`

When enabled (recommended), new configuration options introduced by updates are automatically merged into your existing config.yaml. Existing user-defined values are preserved. Only obsolete internally-managed keys may be replaced or updated when required.

**Default:** `true`

## `show_sudo_warning`

On Linux, the supervisor (start.bin) requires root to bind low ports (< 1024) and manage tmux/screen sessions. When launched from the GUI, authentication is requested automatically via pkexec (graphical prompt). When launched from a terminal, use: sudo ./start.bin Set to false to hide the warning if you have configured your system to handle permissions without root (e.g. using a custom port >= 1024).

**Default:** `true`

## `port_policy`

Controls what happens when a required port is already in use. auto_resolve: true — Automatically find the next free port auto_resolve: false — Log an error and exit (safe mode) session_only: true — Changed ports are used only this session session_only: false — Save resolved ports to config permanently max_offset: 10 — How many ports to try (-1 = unlimited)

- **`auto_resolve`** (default: `true`)
- **`session_only`** (default: `true`)
- **`max_offset`** (default: `10`)

## `api`

The central API server address and port. Interactive API documentation: http://localhost:<port>/docs

- **`port`** — Port that the central API server listens on (default: 29185). Change this if you have another service on the same port (default: `29185`)

## `server_host`

Controls which network interfaces the servers listen on. "127.0.0.1" — Local access only (default, safe) "0.0.0.0" — Allow access from other devices on your network "<IP>" — Bind to a specific network interface Interactive API documentation: http://localhost:<api.port>/docs

**Default:** `"127.0.0.1"`

## `api_key`

Optional API key for authentication when the server is exposed beyond localhost. When set, all non-localhost requests must include the header: X-API-Key: <your_api_key> Leave empty to disable authentication (safe when server_host is 127.0.0.1).

**Default:** `""`

## `control_method`

How the tool communicates with your streaming software. DCS (Direct Control System) — RECOMMENDED Best performance, lowest latency, full feature access. Use with: OBS Studio, vMix, Streamlabs Desktop. ICS (Interface Control System) Uses graphical interface. Slower, fewer features. Required for: TikTok Live Studio, Twitch Studio.

**Default:** `DCS`

## `shutdown`

When enabled, the tool shuts down automatically after your live stream ends. A countdown gives you time to cancel (type 'stop' in the console).

- **`enabled`** (default: `true`)
- **`delay_seconds`** (default: `30`)

## `mc_version`

The Minecraft server version to use (PaperMC build). SAFE versions: 26.3 (tested & confirmed working, default), 1.21.11 (tested & confirmed working). Other versions are UNTESTED and may break functionality. Managed by the Web GUI (Advanced Settings). Do not edit manually.

**Default:** `"26.3"`

## `java`

- **`path`** — Custom Java executable path (optional). If set, this path is used instead of searching the system PATH. Example: "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25\bin\java.exe" (Windows) Example: "/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk/bin/java" (Linux) (default: `""`)
- **`xms`** — RAM allocation. 'G' = Gigabytes. Using the same value for xms (initial) and xmx (maximum) is recommended. Default: 4G — reduce to 2G or 1G if your system has less than 8 GB RAM. Low RAM may cause lag, slow chunk loading, or server crashes (default: `4G`)
- **`xmx`** (default: `4G`)
- **`port`** — Minecraft server port (default: 25565) (default: `25565`)

## `rcon`

RCON allows the tool to send commands to the Minecraft server. IMPORTANT: Keep this enabled — disabling it breaks most functionality.

- **`enabled`** (default: `true`)
- **`password`** — Set a secure password. The tool will ask you to set one on first start if this is left empty (default: `""`)
- **`port`** — RCON port (default: 25575) (default: `25575`)
- **`http_command_api`** — Direct RCON command endpoint (POST /api/v1/rcon/command) for the dashboard console and extensions. Disabled by default for security and stability — direct commands bypass the bridge's RCON queue and throttling. Set to true to enable it (the dashboard Console tab needs it); the queue path keeps working either way (default: `false`)

## `tiktok`

- **`user`** — Your TikTok username — without the @ symbol (default: `your_tiktok_username`)
- **`reconnect_delay_seconds`** — Seconds to wait before attempting to reconnect after a connection loss (default: `30`)
- **`failed_connection_popup_enabled`** — Connection-failure protection. Repeated failed connection attempts can make TikTok block your device for a while. When enabled, after `max_connect_fails` consecutive failed attempts the tool pauses reconnecting and shows a warning in the GUI where you can choose to re-enable the connection or keep it disabled. failed_connection_popup_enabled: true/false (master switch for the popup) max_connect_fails: number of failed attempts before pausing (e.g. 5) (default: `true`)
- **`max_connect_fails`** (default: `5`)
- **`autosave_interval_seconds`** — How often (in seconds) the gift revenue log file is saved to disk. The log is stored at data/gift_revenue_log.jsonl (default: `60`)
- **`diamond_value_usd`** — USD payout per diamond used to estimate gift revenue. Default: 0.004 (creator cash-out per diamond). Adjust to your region/package (default: `0.004`)
- **`follow_tracking`** — Follow tracking — prevents viewers from farming the follow trigger by repeatedly unfollowing and refollowing. Followers are stored in a small SQLite database (fast even with 100K+ entries; legacy .txt lists are imported automatically). mode: "all_time" — Tracks follows across ALL streams (default). Once a user is recorded, their future follows are ignored — even after restarting the tool. "per_stream" — Resets the tracked list every time the tool starts. Each stream starts fresh. NOTE: Only new follows that happen while the tool is running AND connected to a live stream are tracked. Users who already followed before the tool was running cannot be detected — they will trigger a follow action the first time they follow during a tracked stream
  - **`mode`** (default: `"all_time"`)
- **`like_rate_limit`** — Like rate limiting — caps how many likes a single viewer can contribute to the like counter per rolling minute. This prevents a single account from farming like-trigger milestones by spamming likes. enabled: false — Default: disabled. max_per_user_per_minute: 500 — Maximum likes counted per viewer in any rolling 60-second window. Set to 0 for an unlimited rate. Likes above the limit are ignored by the like counter (and therefore by like_triggers), but other viewers are unaffected
  - **`enabled`** (default: `false`)
  - **`max_per_user_per_minute`** (default: `500`)

## `gifts`

The gift ID→name database (core/gifts.json) is auto-refreshed from TikTok's official live-gift endpoint at app start (and on demand via the GUI button in the Actions editor). The factory template (defaults/gifts.json) is never modified, so a stale/missing catalog still has a shipped fallback.

- **`auto_sync`** (default: `true`)
- **`source`** — Source: "auto" (official endpoint, then antiops GitHub mirror fallback), "official" (TikTok endpoint only), or "fallback" (antiops mirror only) (default: `"auto"`)

## `like_triggers`

Like triggers fire when the total stream likes reach a threshold. You can define multiple triggers with different intervals. Each entry requires: id — A unique name for this trigger (used in logs) every — Like interval between activations (e.g., 100 = every 100 likes) function — The trigger name used in data/actions.mca (connects config to command) payload — (optional) A label passed with the trigger (default: "Community") enabled — (optional) Set to false to disable without deleting (default: true) Example: With "every: 100" and function "likes", the trigger fires every 100 likes and executes whatever command you wrote for "likes" in actions.mca.

- **`every`** (default: `100`)
  - **`function`** (default: `like_2`)
  - **`payload`** (default: `Community`)
  - **`enabled`** (default: `true`)
  - **`every`** (default: `100_000`)

## `console`

Controls which windows / processes are shown on screen. Changing these affects what you see when the tool starts.

- **`log_level`** — Visibility level: 0 — Off: Hides everything 1 — Silent: Hides console, keeps GUI and overlays (recommended) 2 — Standard: Shows main windows 3 — Advanced: Also shows background services 4 — Debug: Shows all enabled processes 5 — Override: Shows every process (even disabled ones, debugging only) (default: `1`)
- **`visible`** — Show the main console window (default: `true`)
- **`allow_close`** — If true, the script stays open and typing 'exit' shuts down cleanly. If false, programs start and the launcher exits immediately (default: `true`)

## `minecraft_server_api`

--- MINECRAFT SERVER API --- Handles communication between the bridge and the Minecraft server. Required for player death/respawn detection, datapack loading, etc.

- **`api_port`** (default: `29187`)
- **`web_server_port`** (default: `29188`)
- **`queue_pause_on_death`** — Pause the TikTok command queue while the tracked player is dead and resume it on respawn. Disable if a foreign game sends player_death / player_respawn webhooks that must not affect the Minecraft queue (default: `true`)

## `gui`

--- GUI --- The graphical user interface is served by the central API server and displayed in a pywebview window. Set enabled: true to launch the dashboard on startup.

- **`enabled`** (default: `true`)

## `overlay`

The built-in overlay subsystem displays text messages on stream. It runs as a core component, not a plugin.

- **`enabled`** (default: `true`)
- **`display_mode`** — Display mode: overwrite = replace current message; queue = line up messages (default: `overwrite`)
- **`fade_in`** — Fade durations (milliseconds) (default: `500`)
- **`fade_out`** (default: `500`)
- **`max_fails`** — Circuit breaker settings (default: `3`)
- **`cooldown`** (default: `10`)
- **`overlays`** — Named overlay slots (at least "default" is required)
- **`theme`** — Theme colours for the overlay windows
  - **`background`** (default: `"#00FF00"`)
  - **`text`** (default: `"#ffffff"`)

## `outbound`

--- OUTBOUND CHANNELS (WEBHOOKS / DISCORD) --- Forwards live events to external HTTP endpoints (e.g. Discord webhooks). Each channel subscribes to event patterns (tiktok.gift, tiktok.*, ...). Formats: raw - JSON envelope {"type", "data", "timestamp"} discord - Discord webhook payload built from a template with {user}, {type} and any event data placeholder ({comment}, ...)

- **`enabled`** — Master switch for all outbound deliveries (default: `true`)
- **`max_fails`** — Circuit breaker: after max_fails consecutive failed deliveries a channel pauses for cooldown seconds (default: `3`)
- **`cooldown`** (default: `10`)
- **`retries`** — Additional delivery attempts per message and HTTP timeout in seconds (default: `1`)
- **`timeout`** (default: `5`)
- **`channels`**
  - **`url`** (default: `""`)
    - **`events`** (default: `["tiktok.*"]`)
    - **`format`** (default: `"discord"`)
    - **`template`** (default: `"**{user}** triggered *{type}*"`)
    - **`enabled`** (default: `false`)

## `update`

--- AUTO-UPDATER --- Checks for new versions on startup and installs them automatically. It is strongly recommended to keep this enabled. You can also check for updates manually via the API: GET http://localhost:29185/api/v1/updates/check

- **`enabled`** (default: `true`)
- **`auto_install`** — When true, updates are installed automatically on startup. When false, you will be notified in the GUI when an update is available and can install it manually from the Updates tab (default: `true`)
- **`max_update_logs`** — Maximum number of update log files to keep in logs/update_logs/. 0 = delete all logs after each update -1 = never delete logs (default: `20`)

## `plugin_sandbox`

--- PLUGIN SANDBOX --- Restricts plugin subprocess resources to limit the impact of misbehaving or compromised plugins. enabled: true/false to enable sandboxing profile: Built-in profile name: "light", "moderate" or "strict". When set, it overrides the raw values below. Individual plugins can override it via "sandbox_profile" in their plugin.json. max_memory_mb: Maximum RAM per plugin (Linux direct / Windows job) max_cpu_time: Maximum CPU seconds per plugin (Linux only) max_files: Maximum open file descriptors (Linux only) max_processes: Maximum child processes per plugin (Linux only) priority_class: Windows process priority (below_normal / idle)

- **`enabled`** (default: `false`)
- **`profile`** (default: `""`)
- **`max_memory_mb`** (default: `512`)
- **`max_cpu_time`** (default: `3600`)
- **`max_files`** (default: `256`)
- **`max_processes`** (default: `32`)
- **`priority_class`** (default: `"below_normal"`)
